concurrency.boundary_normalization: The adapter dequeues at most one referral on the Unity player loop and invokes ReferralReceived outside the lock.
concurrency.evidence: A callback alone is not evidence of cross-thread access. Here the source explicitly documents a worker-thread writer and a Unity player-loop reader of the pending referral queue protected by _pendingReferralGate.

findings.summary: The adapter's _pendingReferralGate is justified synchronization for the documented worker writer and player-loop reader; event delivery occurs after the lock is released.
The remaining lock, Interlocked, and SemaphoreSlim inventory contains unsupported synchronization and duplicated same-action guards without another named off-main writer.
Ownership is spread across the root presenter, rewards presenter, service, and popup; the root presenter owns feature orchestration.
Inspect and reuse existing project capabilities for result flows, event binding, and shared execution when their actual semantics match.
The rewards-to-root callback and root-owned popup queue create a concrete non-local lifecycle and ordering risk for reward presentation.
